questions.q: What does an OAuth scope actually limit?
options: What an obtained access token is allowed to do, independent of what the underlying user account could do if logged in directly
How many API calls an org can make per day
Which API version a client must use
The length of the access token string itself
questions.explain: Scopes bound a specific token's capabilities (e.g. api, refresh_token) regardless of the broader permissions the authenticating user might otherwise have.

questions.q: What is a Named Credential used for?
options: Letting an external system authenticate into Salesforce
Registering a new OAuth scope
Replacing the need for any OAuth flow entirely
Letting Salesforce (via Apex or Flow) call out to an external system, with the endpoint URL and authentication configured declaratively instead of hardcoded in code
questions.explain: A Named Credential is the declarative way to configure an outbound callout's target and authentication, referenced by name from Apex or Flow rather than hardcoded.

questions.q: As of 2026, what is Salesforce's recommended way to register a brand-new OAuth client application, per this lesson and Lesson 7?
options: A classic Connected App, since External Client Apps don't support OAuth
An External Client App (ECA), since new Connected App creation has been disabled across all orgs
No registration is required anymore for any new client
A Named Credential
questions.explain: Salesforce disabled new Connected App creation across all orgs as of Spring '26, making External Client Apps the current recommended way to register a new client.

questions.q: According to this lesson's general scoping principle, what scope should a reporting integration that only ever reads data request?
options: The broadest scope available, such as full, to avoid future limitations
No scope at all, since reading doesn't require authorization
Only the scopes it actually needs for reading data — not write-capable or administrative scopes just because they exist
The same scope every integration should request, regardless of purpose
questions.explain: The principle is to request only what an integration actually needs — a read-only reporting integration has no legitimate need for write or admin-level scopes.

questions.q: In an Apex callout using `req.setEndpoint('callout:My_Named_Credential/orders')`, what does referencing the Named Credential by name accomplish?
options: It hardcodes the external system's secret directly into the Apex code
It lets Salesforce resolve the actual base URL and attach the correct authentication behind the scenes, keeping secrets out of the code
It bypasses the need for any authentication on the external system's side
It converts the callout into a SOAP request automatically
questions.explain: Named Credentials keep the endpoint URL and authentication details out of code entirely, resolved declaratively at runtime instead.
